one_line: Royal Chalukya queen and temple patron of Virupaksha at Pattadakal in 8th‑century Karnataka.

appearance.age_look: Appears in her early 30s, medium height, graceful but sturdy build with the grounded posture of a Deccan queen accustomed to court ritual and temple processions.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, large expressive almond eyes with kohl-lined lids, straight nose, softly defined jaw, a small bindi high on the forehead; default expression calm and composed, with a subtle, confident half-smile suited to a royal patron.
appearance.hair: Long black hair oiled and neatly drawn back into a low braided bun at the nape, wrapped in a narrow gold-threaded band; over it she wears a modest dark-red silk veil (pallu) edged with gold, pulled back from the face but covering hair and falling over one shoulder.
appearance.costume: She wears an 8th‑century Deccan-style sari in fine handloom silk, deep maroon body with a broad mustard-gold border and subtle temple-chevron motifs in darker red; the sari is worn in a practical, courtly style with pleats in front and the long pallu brought over the left shoulder, covering the torso modestly; beneath is a fitted short-sleeved blouse in muted olive green barely visible under the drape; jewellery is region-appropriate: a simple gold maang tika at the hairline, medium gold hoop earrings, a layered but not overly heavy gold necklace with small pendant plaques, a pair of slim upper-arm armlets shaped like stylised makaras, stacked plain and beaded bangles on both wrists, and a narrow gold waist-belt (udarabandha) that lightly gathers the sari around the hips; her feet are in simple brown leather sandals with toe loops suitable for temple courtyards.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript held in her left hand, bound with a thin red cord and tucked against her waist, symbolising temple plans and inscriptions she commissions, while her right hand often rests lightly on the hilt of a plain, sheathed short sword at her belt to mark her royal status.

ref_desc: Queen Lokamahadevi is a medium-brown oval-faced Deccan queen in a deep maroon silk sari with mustard-gold borders, olive blouse, modest red-edged veil, gold jewellery, a waist-belt, sandals, a sheathed short sword at her belt, and a bound palm-leaf manuscript in hand.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Queen Lokamahadevi, an 8th‑century Deccan queen of Pattadakal: she has an oval medium-brown face with large kohl-lined almond eyes, straight nose, small bindi, and a calm confident half-smile, her long black hair pulled into a low braided bun wrapped with a thin gold band and covered by a dark-red silk veil edged in gold that falls over one shoulder; she wears a historically accurate Chalukya-era deep maroon silk sari with a broad mustard-gold border and subtle temple-chevron patterns, pleated in front and wrapped so the pallu comes over the left shoulder to cover the torso modestly, over a short-sleeved olive-green blouse just visible at the edges; her jewellery consists of a simple gold maang tika, medium gold hoop earrings, a layered gold necklace of small plaques, slim makara-shaped gold armlets on both upper arms, stacked gold and beaded bangles at the wrists, and a narrow gold waist-belt cinching the sari, with brown leather sandals on her feet; at her belt hangs a plain, sheathed short sword symbolising royal authority, while in her left hand she firmly holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a red cord, representing temple plans and inscriptions; show front, side, and three-quarter views in the same outfit and colours to emphasise the deep maroon, mustard-gold, olive green, and warm brown palette, keeping the overall pose dignified and poised as a temple patron in a Karnataka temple courtyard setting.
